extracted_by: hand, T-0292 — the Democrat read, October 1834
note: Vol. I No. 44. Pages 1-2 are national and foreign reprint; the town is on pages 3 and 4. THE MONTH'S MOST IMPORTANT MATTER IS IN THIS ISSUE and it is not an advertisement: page 3 column 1 carries the Town Ordinance to Prevent Fires of 20 September 1834, which divides Chicago into four wards by street and by river and names a fire warden for each. That column is the Tesseract fallback and it lost two or three characters off the left of every line, so the ward boundaries are read with bracketed supplies and the two unreadable wardens are left unminted.

[At a meeting] of the President and [Trustees of the town] of Chicago, held at the Pre[sbyterian church in said] town, on the 20th day of [September …] the following Ordinance was [passed] […] Be it Ordained by the Board of Trustees […] that said town be and [it is hereby] divided into f[ou]r s[e]parate [wards …] the first ward shall include [all that part] with[in] the incorporated limits of [Chicago …] east of the centre of Lasalle [street …] Jackson and South Water [stree]ts. [The second ward shall] include all that part with[in the incorporated] limits of said town lying [west of the] centre of Lasalle street, and within [… of] […] street. The third Ward [shall include all that] part within the incorpora[ted limits of said] town lying north of the Chica[go river. The fourth] Ward shall include all [that part within] the incorporated limits of said [town … west] of the […] and south branch[…] [of the] Chicago [ri]ver.
claims.notes: THE TOWN'S FOUR WARDS, defined by streets and by the river, and the earliest ward geography this corpus carries. The Vision reading dropped the left edge of every line in this column and the Tesseract fallback that replaced it lost the first two or three characters, so the supplies in `normalized` are bounded to what the surviving text and the ordinance's own grammar support: 'east of the centre of Lasalle [street]' and 'north of the Chica[go river]' are supported, the second ward's western boundary street is NOT and is left '[…]' rather than guessed. Nothing here is minted as a street record — this is the ordinance's own text, and the boundary readings need a second witness before a line can be drawn from them. claims.notes: A SECOND ORDINANCE OF THE SAME SITTING, and two facts in it are worth the card: the trustees met AT THE TREMONT HOUSE on 29 September 1834, and the town had a SUPERVISOR OF ROADS whose permission was needed before earth or sand could be taken off a street. The second is the first sign in this corpus that Chicago's street surfaces were a maintained public thing rather than open ground. The meeting place is read as the Tremont House from 'ot House' plus the issue of 1834-10-29, which prints the trustees meeting 'at the Tre.' House on 13 October; the fire ordinance three columns earlier met at the Presbyterian church, so the two are not interchangeable and this one is bracketed. claims.notes: ONE IMPRESSION OF THE STANDING LAKE STREET LAND-AGENCY CARD. The Democrat sets this advertisement, word for word the same, in every issue from 1834-05-14 to 1834-10-01 — twenty consecutive weeks, eighteen of which set the line ‘purchased and Sold, or by commi[s]sion’ recognisably (T-1051). The card is identified by its copy and not by its display line: the same trade (‘House and Land Agent’), the same offer of building lots in the town and the School Section, the same houses to let, and the same office on Lake street opposite Dr. Temple's. THE LAST IMPRESSION OF THE RUN the corpus can read: the card is not in the Democrat after this issue. The display line is lost — 3261 closes J. K. Botsford's notice immediately above. THE PROPRIETOR'S NAME IS NOT READ HERE and none is supplied into the quote: the record's ‘W. G. Blanchard’ stands on T-0408's reading of the two impressions whose columns are NOT Tesseract fallbacks (1834-07-16 line 5527, 1834-09-17 line 3292) and on identity.json's declared firm merge, not on this impression. The street did not survive the margin and the lines are set out of order (the address at 3266 above 'Housee to Let.' at 3267), so the anchor is read and the street left null. AND IT MATTERS TO A REFUSAL THIS CLAIM DOES NOT TOUCH: identity.json's `refused_firm_merges` holds 'W. G. Blanchard' apart from 'G. Blanshard' partly on the reading that the two cards run in succession rather than together — 'a gap between the two runs rather than an overlap'. This issue is 1834-10-01, the same issue in which 'G. BLANSHARD' is set whole in the stray-horse reward notice that refusal cites, and the Blanshard land card first runs a week later on 1834-10-08. That is a fact about the weeks, recorded here where it was found. The refusal is NOT reopened by this claim and nothing here is merged: what the overlap is worth is a question for the file that owns it.
